about: A realm's standing military by its size, wealth and kind (the owner's order 95, D-194; order 13's feudal armies; order 93's level anchors). Read by src/war/9999978-standing (A.MIL). Regular soldiers: the realm's people x its kind's rate, never under the floor for a realm of floorPop people or more, and never more than its purse keeps: its income x the kind's pay share / upkeep (the release's 3.2 suns a man a year), held to cap. Knights: people / perKnight x the realm's wealth (its income a head against wealthMid, as a square root, held to wealthClamp), held between the kind's least and most, and never fewer than its orders' brethren and a household; dealt to the crown (crownShare), the elite orders (their members) and the houses by rung (rungs), largest remainder first. Levels: data/power.json's ladder, read through A.POWER: soldiers in 80-180, knights 230-299 with pastShare of them past 300, the elite 300-420, each set inside its band by the realm's quality (its troops' quality, its drill, its wealth). The elite are the realm's best ten or so fighters: the people of the realm who stand at 300 or more (an order's master, a General), filled to the count by named champions kept as seeds (no person is made for them).

empire.why: an empire keeps its frontier hosts and the emperor's own legions

kingdom.why: a kingdom keeps the crown's regiments and its lords' companies

collapsing kingdom.why: a kingdom at war with itself keeps every man it can pay

theocracy.why: a church keeps temple guards and the knights of its faith, and few regiments

sultanate.why: a sultan keeps his household slaves-at-arms and his emirs' horse

emirate.why: an emir keeps his household and his sheikhs' riders

merchant republic.why: a republic of merchants keeps a city watch and hires the rest

city-state.why: a free city keeps its walls manned and its guilds drilled

city league.why: a league of cities keeps each city's watch

mountain confederation.why: the valleys keep their own companies, bound by oath to one another

nomad confederation.why: every man of the tents rides and the herds feed the host

orc horde.why: every grown orc fights and the host lives off what it takes

orc clans.why: every grown orc fights for his clan

elven realm.why: the elves are few and long-lived, and every one of them keeps a bow

dwarven hold.why: a hold arms every clan for its gates and its deeps

giant territory.why: the giants are few; one in sixty of them is a warrior, and each is worth a company

pirate haven.why: every man of the port can hold a blade, and the prize money pays them

raceBands.about: A giant's body is another scale (an ordinary grown giant is worth 12 to 30 conscripts: levels about 430 to 540 on A.POWER's ladder), so a giant hold's warriors, its picked ones and its champions stand in bands of their own.

quality.about: The realm's quality, 0 to 1, that sets each level inside its band: a base, its troops' quality (armyQ, the release's: most realms 0.9 to 1.1, the elven, dwarven and giant hosts above), the drill of its forces (forces.xp, 0 to 200), its wealth a head (against wealthMid) and its people (a dwarf's or an elf's body and years). Each part [from, to, weight], summed and held to 0..1: a common realm stands near the middle of each band, a rich and drilled one near the top (its elite near 420).

roles: the master-at-arms of the royal guard
a captain of the household knights
a knight of the tourney lists
the champion of a great house
a captain of the crown's lances
a free lance in the crown's pay
a hedge knight of great name

decide.about: Each AI crown, once a year, weighs raising regiments toward its normal host, keeping what it has, or cutting regiments (A.WHY, kind 'standing'). The reasons are log-odds weights; the decision sets the host the release's recruiting fills (A.forcesAI).
